title: Redwood Migration Demo: OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood API (parity)
summary: Product walkthrough focused on mapping OpenAI/Anthropic/Together API semantics to Redwood API, discussing streaming, function calls, embeddings parity, latency/cost tradeoffs, and security requirements for a healthcare POC.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private deployment
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jake Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Michael Lee (Satori Head of ML), Aisha Khan (Satori Sec Eng), Tom Wu (Satori Platform)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough): Demo of Redwood API focusing on parity with OpenAI/Anthropic/Together. Discussed routing, latency, cost, and security for a healthcare POC. Next steps: share parity spreadsheet, security docs, run benchmarks.

[00:00] Jake Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining  uh this is Jake from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Priya's our solutions engineer, we'll do a quick migration walkthrough. Michael, Aisha, Tom, thanks for carving out time.
[00:14] Michael Lee: Yep thanks Jake, excited  we want to see how close Redwood is to our current OpenAI setup, especially function calls and streaming, that's like 60% of our realtime flows.
[00:25] Priya Desai: Great, we'll map parity first, then demo the API and console. Quick note: transcripts sometimes mistranscribe product names, so when I say "KV cash" I mean KV cache.
[00:36] Aisha Khan: ha, ok noted. Also security first  SOC 2, SSO, and KMS are gating for us. We'll need network diagrams.

[02:10] Priya Desai: Alright slide one: parity approach. We treat OpenAI/Anthropic/Together as source APIs and map request params to Redwood. Example: model -> model_name field, temperature -> temp, max_tokens -> max_tokens, function calling semantics are supported via Redwood's structured tool output. Some differences: Anthropic has sibling safety tokens, Together has different stream chunk formats, but we provide adapters.
[02:50] Tom Wu: Are adapters runtime or config? We don't want a middleware shim that increases latency.
[03:04] Priya Desai: Good q. We do adapters at the API gateway level as lightweight routing transforms  negligible added latency, and for POC we can use our open-source client shim to keep everything local during testing.
[03:20] Michael Lee: Streaming  what's your chunking? OpenAI streams delta tokens with role/finish_reason. How does Redwood compare?
[03:35] Priya Desai: Redwood streams token deltas similarly, we also support structured events for function/tool calls. In practice the client sees a near-identical stream: role markers, token deltas, and a final completion event. In a few cases the transcript generator mangles the role name, but the raw event stream is stable.

[06:00] Jake Morales: Quick demo. Priya, do you want to share your screen? (screen shares)
[06:14] Priya Desai: I'm hitting the Redwood API with a sample echo prompt that's been mapped from an OpenAI request.
[06:25] [screen share shows code snippet]
[06:28] Priya Desai (reading): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"redwood-3-large", "prompt":"Summarize patient intake note" , "temperature":0.2, "stream":true }'
[06:50] Console: you can see streaming tokens arriving; function call example below where we pass tools param.
[07:12] Michael Lee: That looks close. About embeddings  we use both text-embedding-3 and some fine-tuned encoders on Together. What's your equivalent?
[07:30] Priya Desai: We expose multiple embedding models, including open-model variants; for custom encoders we support bringing your own model in Dedicated/Private or using a fine-tune/adapter layer for mapping vector dims. We'll include a mapping doc with dims and distances.
[08:05] Aisha Khan: On data retention  our policy requires no retention for PHI. How does Redwood handle request/response logs?
[08:20] Jake Morales: By default hosted has configurable retention and redaction. For POC we can enable "no retention" and run through Dedicated or Private for full control. We support KMS for envelope encryption and HSM integrations for key custody.
[08:42] Aisha Khan: Good. Also need SSO, RBAC, audit logs  can those be exported to our SIEM?
[08:50] Priya Desai: Yes, audit logs export via syslog/S3 hooks; SAML SSO and SCIM are supported. We'll attach the SOC2/ISO packet and network diagram.

[11:00] Tom Wu: Can you talk throughput? We have bursts ~1.2k reqs/s for inference spike, average 300 qps. Latency SLO is sub 300ms for short prompts.
[11:20] Priya Desai: For small prompts on GPUs we hit p50 ~120ms local token latency; p95 depends on batching. For guaranteed burst handling we recommend Dedicated with auto-burst and fallback routing to hosted variants when capacity constrained. We'll run a benchmark with your sample distribution.
[12:00] Michael Lee: Any caveats around batching and output ordering? We've had concat reorder issues on another platform.
[12:15] Priya Desai: We do continuous batching with sequence-aware ordering; KV cache handling is per-session so it preserves ordering. Occasionally we've seen misattributed speaker tokens in noisy transcripts but that's unrelated to inference ordering.

[15:30] Jake Morales: Now parity mapping specifics. Priya, walk through the spreadsheet?
[15:36] Priya Desai: Sure  link in chat: https://redwood.company/decks/migration-parity.pdf (demo table). Example rows: OpenAI param "n" -> Redwood "num_outputs"; "stop" -> "stop_sequences"; Anthropic "max_tokens_to_sample" -> Redwood "max_tokens". For Together we map streaming chunk ids to Redwood event ids. We'll share the CSV so you can run automated mapping in your client.
[17:10] Michael Lee: Will this require code changes in our backend? We prefer minimal changes in the adapter layer.
[17:20] Priya Desai: Minimal  mostly field renames and optional response parsing for function call JSON. We provide SDKs in node/python that mirror OpenAI semantics where possible to reduce friction.

[19:00] Aisha Khan: If we go Private, does Redwood still provide the control plane? We need an on-prem air-gapped option but with the same console features.
[19:12] Jake Morales: Two options: VPC deployment where the control plane is customer-managed but we provide the console endpoints, or full on-prem package for air-gapped with a local console. Both support audited logs and KMS integration. We'll note the differences in the security doc.

[22:40] Priya Desai: Demo: function calling. Sending a tool schema and getting structured JSON back  (shows example) calling `get_patient_record` returns JSON with id, notes, and risk flags. The Redwood tool output includes metadata fields for provenance which you can disable for PHI-sensitive flows.
[23:15] Michael Lee: That provenance metadata  is that stored by default? We need it off for PHI flow.
[23:24] Priya Desai: It's optional; default in hosted is on for debugging but for PII/PHI flows we recommend disabling and using Private/Dedicated where metadata is kept customer-side.

[26:00] Tom Wu: Networking firewall question  can we restrict egress to our VPC only?
[26:08] Jake Morales: Yes, with Private deployment you control egress. With Dedicated you can request VPC peering and have strict egress rules. Hosted can be configured w restrictive egress via proxying but less common.

[29:30] Michael Lee: Cost  how does Redwood price compare to OpenAI for both gen and embedding?
[29:40] Jake Morales: Pricing varies by model/throughput. Generally our per-token for comparable open models is 20-35% cheaper than OpenAI for high volume, but Dedicated committed pricing yields the biggest delta. We'll send a tailored pricing spreadsheet for your usage profile.
[30:10] Michael Lee: We also use Together for some lower-cost bulk tasks. Is there a path to use Together model weights on Redwood Dedicated?
[30:25] Priya Desai: You can bring your own model artifacts on Dedicated/Private, subject to licensing. For Together-hosted models we provide adapters; for self-hosted weights we'll help with onboarding.

[33:00] Aisha Khan: One more on compliance: we need monthly penetration test reports and an SOC2 Type II report with last 12 months.
[33:10] Jake Morales: We'll attach SOC2 Type II and our latest security audit summary. For pen tests we can provide our scope and results. If you require vendor-managed pen test windows we can coordinate.

[36:00] Priya Desai: Ok near the end  POC proposal. 4-week pilot: week 1 mapping and small integration test, week 2 run 10k sample requests and streaming verification, week 3 scale benchmark to your burst profile with Dedicated trial, week 4 results review and next steps. Deliverables: parity spreadsheet, benchmark results, security packet.
[36:30] Michael Lee: Sounds good. Estimated costs for Dedicated trial?
[36:38] Jake Morales: We'll provide an estimate in the pricing sheet; short trials often covered by Redwood credits, we can discuss on contract.

[39:00] Tom Wu: Any gotchas with rate limits during burst tests? We need hard limits and graceful 429 handling.
[39:12] Priya Desai: You'll get explicit rate limit headers and can configure per-tenant quotas; we support retry/backoff advisories and graceful fallback routing to a cheaper model if desired.

[42:00] Jake Morales: Ok final recap  Jake: share parity CSV, pricing, security docs. Priya: run benchmark with Satori sample prompts (Priya to coordinate with Tom) and deliver results. Aisha: send the required compliance checklist items.
[42:25] Michael Lee: I'll get legal involved after the pilot terms; Aisha will own security.
[42:35] Aisha Khan: Yep. Target dates?
[42:40] Jake Morales: We'll aim to have docs and parity spreadsheet by EOD 2026-07-02, benchmark kickoff by 2026-07-06, and initial results by 2026-07-13.
[44:00] Tom Wu: Great thanks.
[44:08] Jake Morales: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and the POC plan.

End of transcript.
